issue_context.title: Add APIs to make nint & nuint match Int32 and Int64
comments: I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

Tagging subscribers to this area: @tannergooding, @pgovind See info in area-owners.md if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
## Background and Motivation Almost all numeric types have `Parse` and `TryParse` ReadOnlySpan overload, I think it's good for `nint` to have them too. ## Proposed API ```diff namespace System { public class IntPtr { + public static IntPtr Parse(ReadOnlySpan s) { } + public static IntPtr Parse(ReadOnlySpan s, NumberStyles style, IFormatProvider? provider) { } + public static bool TryParse(ReadOnlySpan s, out IntPtr result) { } + public static bool TryParse(ReadOnlySpan s, NumberStyles style, IFormatProvider? provider, out IntPtr result) { } } ``` ## Usage Examples ## Alternative Designs ## Risks
Author: Cyl18
Assignees: -
Labels: `api-suggestion`, `area-System.Numerics`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -

> To match what's on Int32 and Int64, instead of:
> 
> ```cs
> public static IntPtr Parse(ReadOnlySpan<char> s) { }
> public static IntPtr Parse(ReadOnlySpan<char> s, NumberStyles style, IFormatProvider? provider) { }
> ```
> 
> I think we'd want:
> 
> ```cs
> public static IntPtr Parse(ReadOnlySpan<char> s, NumberStyles style = NumberStyles.Integer, IFormatProvider? provider = null)
> ```

I agree with you, and I've changed my proposal:)

> Can I try to PR this myself? :)

Definitely. I tend to mark most of the `area-System.Numerics` issues as `up-for-grabs` once approved and then anyone is free to comment that they'd like to pick it up 😄 

I'm happy to answer any questions if you have them and let me know if you get stuck.

@tannergooding I noticed that `TryFormat` was already being implemented, so the proposal might need to be changed
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14993992/106186671-8dd3c780-61df-11eb-94bd-5e717d3cb5b7.png)

It's implemented, but internal explicitly done and therefore private since `ISpanFormattable` is `internal`

The API should just become `public bool TryFormat`, as is done for `Int32` and others

> It's implemented, but internal explicitly done and therefore private since `ISpanFormattable` is `internal`
> 
> The API should just become `public bool TryFormat`, as is done for `Int32` and others

(Int32)
![Int32](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14993992/106188206-a218c400-61e1-11eb-8352-66587697eab6.png)
(Change)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14993992/106188338-d1c7cc00-61e1-11eb-8a19-b81573fbc8d5.png)

Is it okay to just add a `public` to `TryFormat`? It's like what in `Int32`

> Is it okay to just add a public to TryFormat? It's like what in Int32

Yes, but you'll also want to tweak the signature to add the default arguments..

review_comments:
It looks like the failures for this one are because `Parse_ValidWithOffsetCount_TestData` is casting `offset` and `count` to `IntPtr`, which isn't correct given they are used as part of `AsSpan`.

Looks like this is a pre-existing failure and the test data wasn't being used until this PR
So I just remove these casts?

Right, you would remove the cast from the second and third argument, but not from the last. https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/47595/files/b2c52b2a7dc13feae2001a55721e39bba2dccf82#diff-0b1f3c3826a374c251afa76e3234f9c10aeda984ded5d726262545c955014697R847, for example, would become: `yield return new object[] { "2147483647", 1, 9, NumberStyles.None, null, (IntPtr)147483647 };` so they types match the expected
Nit: the string-based routines are above the test data.  Can you please move these span-based tests to co-locate them with the corresponding string-based ones?

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14993992/106290415-6800fe00-6285-11eb-9271-b1643530d634.png)
I think they were already corresponding the string-based ones?

I talked with @stephentoub briefly offline and he was suggesting that the new span-based `Parse`/`Format` tests and test data be moved next to the string-based variants of the same

None of the other primitive types (like `Int32`) currently match this and so we decided not to block, but it seems like a good low priority/up-for-grabs issue if someone else feels like the consistency would help.
Preexisting your change, but it's not obvious to me staring at this now what here requires this be `unsafe`?

If I remove `unsafe`, it would become not compilable:
